parsed_response.causal_explanation: A collision is confirmed by the oracle around 47.125 s. In the preceding window the ego has nonzero speed per the collision-window summary, a nearby simulator object (~3.1 m away), active perception/prediction outputs, and a full set of final waypoints marked unblocked with a reported closest_object_distance of 0.0. However, vehicle_cmd target speed, accel, brake, and steer commands remain zero throughout the trace summary, while vehicle_status in the collision window reports nonzero throttle and velocity. This mismatch between command and status, plus incomplete motion data (global odometry shows almost no displacement while collision-window speed is several m/s), prevents a clear module-level attribution. The dataset indicates an additional lane-invasion symptom, but the error.json oracle does not, so lane invasion cannot be treated as confirmed.
parsed_response.root_cause_pattern: Conservative preservation pattern: a collision occurs while a nearby actor is present and planning/perception topics are populated, but high-level control commands are effectively zero and module-level responsibility (including any lane invasion) remains unknown due to inconsistent motion and oracle information.

A non-ego object is present about 3.128 m from the ego before collision, indicating a nearby actor at impact time.

Vehicle_cmd topic exists but accel_cmd, brake_cmd, steer_cmd, and target_speed are all zero across the sampled interval.

Odometry start and end positions are almost identical, suggesting little net displacement despite the collision-window report of several m/s pre-collision speed.
Detection and prediction topics are present throughout the scenario and report at least one object, including labels such as person and unknown, indicating ongoing perception of actors.
